answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 5 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The pigment multiplier is published, charged in lagoon, and ember lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 1219 identities would post 1307 proofs and burn roughly 85 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
